MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

Positioned right after a determiner/preposition/verb slot, this neuron fires on non-article continuations — typically word-initial sub-word fragments or content words (" M"aserati, " pl"umps, " PO"E, " pe"acemaking, " full") — while being strongly *suppressed* when that same slot is filled by the definite article "the"/"there", so it effectively signals "this slot is not 'the'".

L6·N13601unmasked layer
This appears to be a low-magnitude, weakly-selective "function word" neuron: its peaks land on ordinary high-frequency determiners/prepositions/pronouns ("a", "the", "at", "are", "It") in the middle of fluent, conversational how-to/informational prose, and the very same tokens ("the", "You", ",") can drive it strongly negative — so there is no consistent semantic trigger, only context-dependent modulation on common function-word positions.
